---
title: "check-key-equations-displayed.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that fails when a pull request adds an inline equation
in a proof that should be in display math.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-28) is that a key equation goes in a display,
never inline.
A key equation is a theorem's conclusion,
an equation a proof builds toward,
or an equation a later step refers to.

This is a partial heuristic,
because no script can know which equation a reader should remember.
It looks only inside a proof div (`.proof`, `proof` or an id starting `prf-`)
and flags an inline equation in two cases:

- it restates a displayed equation (`$$ ... $$`) of the same file,
  which is the parent theorem's statement in a one-div-per-file layout;
- it contains a relation (`=`, `<`, `>`, `\le`, `\ge`, `\neq` or `\approx`),
  ends its sentence,
  and follows "yields", "gives", "implies", "so", "thus", "hence",
  "therefore" or "forces",
  or the next line opens with "So", "Hence", "Therefore" or "Thus".

It misses a key equation with no cue word, and it may flag a minor step.
Put `<!-- inline-ok -->` on the line to accept an inline equation.
Code fences, inline code and HTML comments are skipped,
and an equation split over two lines is not seen.

An untouched line is never reflagged.
With no base ref, as on a `push` event, the check skips
instead of scanning the whole tree;
`whole-tree` measures a corpus.

## Usage

Copy
[`examples/check-key-equations-displayed.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-key-equations-displayed.yml)
to `.github/workflows/` in your repository.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | `*.qmd` | Space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check |
| `fail` | `true` | Fail the workflow on a finding instead of warning |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Scan every proof, not only a PR's additions |
| `runs-on` | `ubuntu-latest` | Runner label; self-hosted only for a private repository |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version to set up |
